name: remove-item-then-refresh
notes: sequence + advanceOn: the list endpoint answers with three items until a DELETE arrives, then with two. Because the trigger is the DELETE rather than the list rule's own calls, the screen can fetch the list as many times as it likes — a prefetch, a re-render, a pull-to-refresh on appear — without moving the scenario on. That is the difference between this and a plain step-per-call sequence, which the first extra fetch would desynchronise. onExhausted is repeatLast so a second delete leaves the list where it is rather than answering 500.
